newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Latin King gang leader gets life term.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Latin King gang leader gets life term.

text.p: The leader of the New York chapter of the Latin Kings, the city's largest street gang, was sentenced Friday to life in prison without parole for masterminding a violent murder spree that left nine dead.
Luis Felipe, 34, had been convicted by Manhattan federal jury in November of 18 counts of racketeering and firearms charges.

The evidence presented at his trial showed that between May 1993 and June 1994, the Latin Kings, under Felipe's direction, was responsible for a series of murders, attempted murders, arsons, armed robberies and beatings that left at least nine people dead and numerous others seriously injured.
Over 40 other members of the Latin Kings have pleaded guilty for their roles in the crimes.
U.S. District Judge John Martin said that Felipe is so ruthless that he would have imposed the death penalty if it was an option in the case.

"Not as a punishment because I don't personally believe in the death penalty as a punishment but I would impose it as the only foolproof means of preventing this defendant from ordering murders in the future.
"This defendant has absolutely no regard for human life and he obviously enjoys a god-like role in determining who should live and who die."

Martin, who imposed a 45-year prison term in addition to the life sentence, set special incarceration conditions that prohibit Felipe from having contact with other prisoners and prevent him from having telephone contact with anyone.
"This defendant has forfeited any right to human contact," he said.

The Latin Kings gang was formed in the 1940s by Latino inmates in Chicago jails. Felipe, who is known as King Blood, founded the New York chapter in 1986 while he was imprisoned in Helmuth, New York. It is estimated that the Latin Kings has some 2,000 members across the state.
